summary.headline: GPT Healthcare Q2 FY27 revenue rose 14.1% to ₹135.6 crore and EBITDA margin expanded 150 bps to 21.5%, while Raipur break-even slipped to Q1 FY28.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations grew 14.1% YoY to ₹135.6 crore, with EBITDA up 23.9% to ₹29.8 crore and PAT up 45.2% to ₹15.4 crore. Growth was attributed to higher inpatient volumes (about 11% at network level) and occupancy rising to 50.3% from 47.4%. H1 FY27 revenue was ₹261.8 crore (+15.8%) with EBITDA of ₹56 crore (+30.3%). Management reaffirmed FY27 growth of about 15-16% but pushed the Raipur break-even timeline out by a quarter, to Q1 FY28, due to clinical attrition from new competition.

segments.name: Dum Dum (largest revenue contributor)
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 revenue ₹84.8 crore, occupancy 69.4%, ARPOB ₹43,086. Cardiac thoracic and vascular surgery unit commenced.

segments.name: Salt Lake (Kolkata)
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 occupancy 65.4% and highest network ARPOB at ₹43,284; grew 12% YoY and crossed 850 robotic surgeries.

segments.name: Howrah
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 revenue grew 25% YoY, occupancy 45.8%; orthopaedic volumes above 120-150 procedures per month; MECO robotic knee system launched, nearing 100 procedures.

segments.name: Agartala (Tripura)
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 ARPOB ₹40,254 and growth of 8.1%; occupancy about 55%, with a target of about 70%. Consultant recruitment is the constraint; expansion possible within existing premises.

segments.name: Raipur (Chhattisgarh)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue about ₹9 crore, occupancy about 16.5%. H1 losses ₹6.5 crore (Q2 about ₹9 crore per the call; wording unclear). FY27 loss guided at about ₹10 crore; break-even at about 35% occupancy now slipped to Q1 FY28.

segments.name: Central India / Jamshedpur (upcoming)
segments.commentary: 155-bed tertiary hospital expected to open March-April 2027; FY28 loss guided at a small amount.

segments.name: Nephrology (Dum Dum)
segments.commentary: Contribution reduced to under 15% of hospital revenue from about 30% earlier.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of about 15-16% YoY reaffirmed.
Raipur break-even on a monthly basis now expected in Q1 FY28, versus earlier Q3 FY27.
Raipur expected to be marginally net positive in FY28; FY27 loss about ₹10 crore.
Average occupancy expected at 25-30% by end of Q4 FY27 for the new hospital(s) (ambiguous; likely Raipur/Jamshedpur ramp-up).
Management targets ROE and ROCE of about 25%.
Agartala and Raipur can each add about 100 beds; Agartala within existing premises, Raipur via additional leased space from developer.
Mature hospitals targeted at about 70% occupancy; Dum Dum and Salt Lake can approach 80% but beyond that is seen as very difficult.
risks_watch: Raipur break-even slipped by a quarter (to Q1 FY28) after clinician attrition to Artemis and other new entrants; monitor occupancy trajectory toward the 35% break-even level.
Competitive intensity in Eastern and Central India (Raipur, Jamshedpur) may pressure doctor retention and productivity.
Supreme Court judgment on trade margins on essential medicines could affect service pricing and margins; clarity expected from November.
Jamshedpur ramp-up (155 beds, March-April 2027) adds losses and debt-funded capex.
Agartala occupancy stuck around 55% due to consultant recruitment constraints.
Q2 ARPOB dipped sequentially; watch whether pricing and mix recover.
summary.management_tone: Confident on core hospital growth and reaffirmed FY27 guidance, but cautious on Raipur, where break-even was pushed back a quarter. Management was evasive on the Q2 Raipur loss figure, which was stated inconsistently, and on the timing of new acquisitions.
key_quotes: So we are committed to our initial estimates of F527 numbers.
We expect the break even to be slightly delayed to quarter one of FY28.
Generally, new tertiary care hospitals end up taking almost three years to break even on a monthly basis.

qa_highlights.question: Why did ARPOB fall sequentially, what drove the Raipur loss for the quarter, and when will Raipur break even?
qa_highlights.answer: ARPOB dip is minor and seasonal (Q2 fever season changed specialty mix). Raipur Q2 loss about ₹9 crore per the call; H1 loss ₹6.5 crore. Monthly break-even now expected by Q1 FY28, after attrition to new competition; new tertiary hospitals typically take about three years.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 guidance intact, and what are the Raipur and Jamshedpur pre-opening/lead expenses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is committed to FY27 estimates and expects about 15-16% revenue growth. Raipur lead expenses about ₹4 crore a year; Jamshedpur expected to be similar.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company thinking about growth and capex, given 70% occupancy targets in mature hospitals?
qa_highlights.answer: Management plans to add hospitals every couple of years; the 155-bed Jamshedpur hospital is due March-April 2027. It is scouting greenfield and acquisition options in Eastern India but will only act on meaningful, suitable deals.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Agartala occupancy lower than older Kolkata hospitals, and is there bed expansion scope there?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited Tripura's remoteness and past consultant recruitment challenges. Consultants are being added and management expects occupancy to reach about 70% soon. Agartala can add beds within existing premises.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company sustain 80%+ occupancy, and how have ALOS trends moved?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 80% is achievable for Dum Dum and Salt Lake but beyond that is very difficult. ALOS at Salt Lake is about 2.9-3 days; Dum Dum ALOS fell from about 5.5 to 4.3 days.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY28 Raipur and Jamshedpur loss expectations and how is competition affecting doctor retention?
qa_highlights.answer: Raipur expected to be marginally net positive in FY28 and FY27 loss about ₹10 crore. Jamshedpur FY28 loss expected to be small. Attrition at Raipur was due to competitor offers (Artemis entry); management is using conferences and clinical engagement to retain consultants.

capex_capacity: 155-bed tertiary care hospital (Jamshedpur, Jharkhand) expected to commence operations in March-April 2027; debt to be used for funding this and newer hospitals alongside equity.
Agartala can add beds within existing premises; Raipur can add space by taking additional leased space from developer. Management says each of Agartala and Raipur can add about 100 beds.
Management is scouting greenfield and acquisition opportunities in Eastern India; no agreement yet, and management said it will not enter deals just for expansion.
Management aims for ROE and ROCE of about 25%, citing disciplined capital allocation, prudent leverage and better returns from existing assets.
Cash and mutual funds about ₹45 crore; total borrowings about ₹35 crore. Raipur FY27 loss about ₹10 crore; Jamshedpur FY28 loss guided at a small amount.
demand_pricing: Q2 FY27 network occupancy 50.3% vs 47.4% YoY; network ARPOB ₹40,721 (+7.1% YoY), but down sequentially per analyst; management attributed the dip to seasonal fever-season specialty mix.
Q2 inpatient volumes up about 11% YoY at network level, driving the occupancy and revenue growth; Dum Dum and Howrah grew at double digits, Salt Lake about 10%.
Mature hospital occupancy: Salt Lake ~68%, Dum Dum ~74%, Agartala ~55% (target ~70%), Howrah ~45.8% (H1). Dum Dum and Salt Lake can approach 80%, beyond which management sees it as very difficult.
Raipur occupancy about 16.5% in Q2; break-even at about 35% occupancy now expected in Q1 FY28 (earlier Q3 FY27). Average occupancy guided at 25-30% by end Q4 FY27.

Pricing: management said pricing is about 10-15% below peers Manipal, Artemis and AMRI at comparable locations. Corporate ARPOB at Raipur is slightly better than Ayushman Bharat; corporate payment cycle within 90 days.
Nephrology at Dum Dum now under 15% of hospital revenue vs about 30% earlier. Oncology partner-led revenue about 4% of Agartala revenue, expected to stabilise at 10-15%.
International patient flow from Bangladesh recovering slowly, with more visa requests but not yet back to historical levels.
Supreme Court judgment on trade margins on essential medicines: impact unclear until order details in November; management intends to correct service pricing to protect margins.

rows.label: Volume growth

rows.label: New capex announcement

rows.label: Guidance upgrade

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Cardiac thoracic and vascular surgery unit at Dum Dum has commenced, and the MECO robotic knee system at Howrah is nearing 100 procedures, with more robotic procedures scaling at Salt Lake.

rows.label: Pricing 10-15% below peers; Supreme Court trade-margin ruling
rows.why: Pricing is 10-15% below Manipal, Artemis and AMRI, and the Supreme Court judgment on essential-medicine trade margins (clarity expected November) could force service-price corrections.

rows.label: Raipur break-even in Q1 FY28
rows.why: Break-even at about 35% occupancy has slipped from Q3 FY27 to Q1 FY28, with occupancy at 16.5% in Q2 and the FY27 loss guided at about ₹10 crore.

rows.label: Eastern India greenfield or acquisition scouting
rows.why: Management is scouting greenfield and acquisition options in Eastern India with no agreement yet and says it will not enter deals just for expansion.

tone.note: Management was confident on core hospitals and reaffirmed 15-16% FY27 growth, but cautious on Raipur, where break-even slipped a quarter; analysts pushed on the ARPOB sequential dip and the inconsistent Raipur Q2 loss figure.
